title: Protocol to study molecule exchange between venous blood and CSF in live mice using transcranial bioluminescence imaging
protocol: Turn on the microscope xyz stage controller.
Turn on the PC for BLI imaging.
Turn on the light-source for BLI imaging.
Turn on the microscope camera for BLI imaging.
Set imaging settings in NIS-Elements.
Format 512 × 512 pixels.
Set speed to 1 Hz (1 s exposure time).
Set gain to 300.
Set gain multiplier to 3×.
Determine the correct pixel size with a ruler.
Note the magnification of the microscope manually.
Prepare the syringe pump.
Break off the sharp tip of a 30G dental needle using a needle holder.
Insert the broken-off tip into 25 cm length of PE10 tubing.
Flush long tubing and attached cannula with aCSF using a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 30G needle.
Remove the syringe, leaving the 30G cannula attached to the rear end of the tubing.
Fit the cannula onto a 100 μL syringe filled with distilled water.
Connect the 100 μL syringe to a syringe pump.
Autoclave tools and ensure a clean, sterile environment before beginning.
Weigh the mouse (15 g-40 g).
Anesthetize the mouse via an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine (100 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg).
Re-dose with half a dose of ketamine (50 mg/kg) and xylazine (5 mg/kg) as needed during the procedure, typically every 40 minutes.
Inject buprenorphine (0.05 mg/kg) subcutaneously for systemic analgesia.
Wait 5-10 minutes after administering buprenorphine.
Place the mouse on a heating pad set to 37°C covered with an absorbent pad once toe pinch reflexes cease.
Shave the mouse's skin.
Clean the shaved area with ethanol, chlorhexidine, and iodine solution.
Cut the skin to expose the skull.
Pinch the toes with surgical tweezers to ensure full anesthesia throughout the procedure.
Monitor respiration and eye movement reflexes continuously.
Shave the head and neck of the mouse.
Remove excess fur from the shaved area.
Sterilize the exposed skin using an ethanol swab first.
Repeat sterilization using chlorhexidine and iodine solution three times.
Apply eye ointment to protect the eyes.
Inject 0.5 mL of lidocaine (0.2 mg/mL) subcutaneously near the neck region.
Inject another 0.5 mL of lidocaine near the scalp; a small bulge will appear after injection.
Wait for 2 minutes for the lidocaine to take effect.
Perform a midline incision along the scalp from the frontal region to the neck region using a scalpel.
Expose the neck muscle using tweezers and scissors.
Gently pull the skin to the sides of the skull with tweezers to expose the skull.
Dry the skull thoroughly.
Remove the periosteum with a cotton swab.
Clean the skull using an ethanol swab followed by 10% ferric chloride solution.
Place a thin layer of transparent cyanoacrylate superglue around the viewing window on one side of the headplate.
Turn the headplate such that the front faces the back.
Carefully place the glue-coated headplate on top of the mouse’s head to position the viewing window above the region of interest.
Apply light pressure to ensure the headplate lies flat onto the head.
Apply a small drop of acrylate along the edges of the headplate to bond the glue.
Check the stability of the headplate by gently and lightly probing it with forceps.
Place the animal with the heating pad into the MAG-1 holder.
Ensure that the head is tightly secured into the holder by gently probing the headplate with forceps under the microscope.
Dry the skull again using a dry cotton swab and compressed air.
Use the drill to gently thin the skull near the lambda region around the transverse sinus.
Alternate between drilling and removing debris with a compressed air bottle.
Test the thickness of the thinned area with blunt end forceps; optimal thickness is approximately 20 μm.
Manipulate light carefully to check visibility of vasculature beneath the skull.
Clean the thinned area by removing all debris and washing with 0.9% saline solution.
Ensure the skull surface is dry before proceeding.
Apply a small drop of cyanoacrylate glue at the caudal end of the brain.
Use a spatula to immediately distribute the glue creating a thin layer covering the entire skull.
Wait 5 min for the glue to dry.
Prepare the cannula and tubing.
Use a needle holder to break off the beveled tip of a 30G dental needle.
Insert the beveled needle into 4 cm length of PE10 tubing.
Flush this short tubing and cannula with aCSF using a 1 ml syringe fitted with a 30G needle.
Remove the animal from the MAG-1 holder and restrain into a stereotaxic frame.
Tilt the head slightly to create a 120° angle.
Expose the cisterna magna using a pair of forceps to separate the neck muscles.
Pierce the cisterna magna at the center of the triangle.
Secure the cannulation by adding a drop of cyanoacrylate glue to the area surrounding the point of entry.
Cover the needle and the surrounding area with dental cement.
Place the animal on the imaging stage ensuring tubing from the pump can reach it.
Attach the syringe pump tubing to the cannula.
Retro-orbitally inject the substrate at an approximately 30° angle.
Lift the skin immediately above the neck muscle using fine tweezers and cut approximately 1 cm above the midline using a pair of scissors.
Use surgical eye spears or cotton swabs to dry the newly exposed area.
Gently remove the connective tissue above the neck muscles using surgical tweezers.
Separate the neck muscles along the midline with a pair of forceps in each hand, exposing the cisterna magna (CM).
Wipe the dural membrane above the CM using a cotton swab.
Retrieve the short tubing prepared in the previous steps.
Remove the attached syringe and 30G needle from the tubing.
Ensure that the tubing remains filled with aCSF and no air bubbles are present.
Identify the area of the CM through dura as a triangle.
Insert approximately 1 mm of the cannula into the center at a 45° angle to the head.
Place the needle at the center of the triangle and gently move it from side to side to loosen the entry point before piercing the dura.
Apply 1–2 drops of cyanoacrylate glue to the area where you have inserted the cannula.
Immediately apply a drop of glue accelerator after applying the glue.
Cover the needle and the surrounding area reaching up to the caudal end of the headplate with a mixture of dental cement and cyanoacrylate glue (2 drops).
Apply a drop of glue accelerator over the covered area.
Seal the tubing with a surgical cauterizer to maintain intracranial pressure levels during transport.
Ensure that the tubing can reach the animal on its MAG-1 holder.
Move the mouse to the imaging area and head fix onto a MAG-1 holder with a heating pad under the macroscope.
Withdraw a bit of air using the syringe pump to insert an air bubble into the long tubing.
Withdraw 12 μL of purified GeNL using the syringe pump.
Ensure that no air bubble is present between the tubing and cannula by infusing a small amount until you see a bit of GeNL at the needle tip.
Cut 1 mm of the short tubing attached to the cannula on the mouse.
Gently insert the long tubing with the sharp dental needle into the small cannula on the mice.
Record for 1 min under white light.
Start the pump to infuse at 1 μL/min for 10 min.
Allow the GeNL to circulate for another 20 min.
Check anesthetic depth of the animal and consider re-dosing if necessary.
Close the curtains/cover around the imaging area to ensure complete darkness before imaging.
Change the filter to FITC/Cy5 and verify the distribution of the enzyme by imaging the mNeongreen fluorescent signal at 490 nm excitation.
Record a representative image.
Remove all filters and record the background intensity for 1 min.
Dilute 25 μL of FFz in 75 μL PBS in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Withdraw a total volume of 100 μL of the diluted FFz using a 0.5 mL insulin needle and syringe.
Ensure all imaging settings are appropriate.
Ensure curtains can be closed easily after the following steps.
Ensure recording can start immediately after retro-orbital injection.
Introduce the cannula at a 30° angle into the medial canthus of the eye with the bevel facing down.
Gently follow the eyeball down until the needle tip reaches the base of the eye.
Slowly inject the substrate using the syringe.
Withdraw the syringe smoothly after injection.
Immediately close the curtains to ensure darkness.
Start a 5-min bioluminescence recording using the same settings as for baseline recording.
Retro-orbitally inject 100 μL of tetramethyl rhodamine dextran (TMR).
Change the filter set of the microscope to DAPI/TRITC.
Record the tracer distribution at 500 nm excitation for 1 min to visualize the vasculature.
